materialChanges: Changed scene-clinical-wrap-up from no-material-claims to claims-mapped, mapped the reused assignment, cohort, randomized-inference, and causal-boundary claims to it, and added a learner-visible source note.
Replaced the unverified PREM-SCI-003 carry-forward statement with a self-contained fictional setup and added a sourced crossover-design claim plus its glossary entry and reference locator.

Made the crossover choice and causal interpretation conditional on ethical and clinically supervised assignment, adherence, comparable measurement, stable or addressed co-interventions, and an explicit carryover, period, and sequence plan, with an observational or narrower-inference fallback.

Added scene-clinical-wrap-up to the glossary mappings for its core vocabulary and corrected attribution and author-assistance wording so historical version provenance is not represented as the current decision.

reviewDispositions.rationale: scene-clinical-wrap-up is now claims-mapped; the assignment, cohort, randomized-inference, and causal-boundary claims map to it; a distinct crossover-design claim was added; and the scene now exposes all supporting claim and source IDs in a learner-visible source note. The unsupported PREM-SCI-003 carry-forward statement was replaced by a self-contained fictional setup because the other lesson was outside this run's inspection boundary.

The crossover choice is now conditional on ethical acceptability, clinical supervision, feasibility, randomized order, adherence, comparable measurement, stable or addressed co-interventions, and an explicit separation or design-and-analysis plan for carryover, period, and sequence effects. The scene directs investigators to another acceptable design or a narrower inference when those conditions fail.

The reviewer confirmed that item-distinguish-cohort-case-control correctly keys source-population and exposure-first entry as retrospective cohort, outcome-first selection as case-control, and record age as non-decisive. The item and rubric were preserved.

The reviewer confirmed that the cutoff transfer correctly treats outside assignment as a natural-experiment candidate, checks manipulation and competing changes, bounds inference near the cutoff, and supplies an association-only observational fallback. That teaching sequence was preserved.
The concrete residence-hall opening and its ordinary-language assignment and timeline questions already pass the cited first-read function, so the opening was preserved unchanged.
The retrospective-cohort worked example already exposes the task, givens, selection plan, execution, alternatives, bounded interpretation, and self-explanation prompt. It was preserved unchanged.
Both misconception blocks already elicit a commitment, explain why the shortcut fails, reconstruct the design rule, and recheck it in a changed case. They were preserved unchanged.
The filtration-grant cutoff task already requires assignment checks, design selection, bounded inference, and an observational fallback in a new context. It was preserved unchanged.

scene-clinical-wrap-up was added to the glossary sceneIds for exposure, outcome, experiment, observational study, cohort study, and causal inference. Random assignment was also linked because the revised scene uses randomized condition order, and crossover experiment was added as a newly defined term.

The misleading use of 'Current' and 'This' for version 0.1.1 was corrected. The attribution now identifies 0.1.1 as an earlier historical finalization and explicitly distinguishes it from the current 0.2.0 decision; changing the historical run's actual version number to 0.2.0 would have falsified provenance.

evidenceChecked: Read all five final scene files in lesson order and checked one level-one heading per scene, logical source order, descriptive headings, and prose explanations for every arrow and table relationship.

Checked the explicit Accessibility and alternatives and Recovery route sections: tasks permit prose, bullets, or tables; are untimed; require no color, audio, image upload, dragging, laboratory access, or personal data; and have actionable retry routes.
Checked assessment.json for untimed retakes, prompt-before-feedback structure, text or single-choice response paths, string-valued acceptableResponses, reasoning-rich feedback, and remediation.
Checked the final Markdown for raw HTML, HTML entities, scripts, event handlers, remote embeds, data URLs, and sensory-only or pointer-only instructions; none are present.
Checked every claims-mapped scene against claims.json and its learner-visible source note, including complete scene-clinical-wrap-up coverage for the new crossover claim and all reused claims.

Checked all four reference records for allowed source types, HTTPS locations, factual-reference uses, facts-only-original-expression rights bases, concrete rights evidence, dated checked-no-agent-restriction-found access records, and absence of human-only sources.

Checked lesson.json and ATTRIBUTION.md for accountable authorship, material agent disclosure, CC BY 4.0 licensing, historical provenance, original-synthesis attestation, and an empty thirdPartyAssets list.

Checked the fictional-case, privacy, and clinical boundaries: the lesson contains no participant data, medical efficacy claim, treatment recommendation, unsafe experiment, or credential claim, and the crossover case now requires ethical acceptability and clinical supervision.
limitations: This was a static source audit; no browser rendering, representative screen-reader session, keyboard-only traversal, 200% zoom/reflow, reduced-motion, print, or planned non-web export was executed.
No real learner testing was performed, consistent with the learning-design review's limitation.

Remote source pages and current terms were not re-fetched in this run. The audit relied on the dated access and rights records plus the academic review, whose direct full-text access encountered interstitial and HTTP limitations.

Per the operator's scope, files under site were not opened and npm validation or source preflight was not run. Local structural checks covered JSON parsing, identity and version consistency, field dates and lengths, assessment answer types, link integrity, source-note coverage, prohibited Markdown constructs, review-input consistency, and finalizer-run freshness.

rationale: The exact original candidate and both eligible advisory records were read. The academic request-changes findings identified a real same-scene evidence gap and overbroad crossover inference; the bounded final revision resolves both without changing lesson identity, version, status, assessment logic, or unaffected teaching. The learning-design approval is preserved, its two metadata findings are resolved, and every one of the ten indexed findings has a disposition. The resulting pack is coherent, self-contained, academically bounded, accessible through source-equivalent routes, and rights-compliant on the recorded evidence. The quorum snapshot counts the two disclosed artifacts and the supplied non-dismissed COMMENTED transports: one academic request-changes and one learning-design approval, across two distinct declared runs and model/provider families but one accountable principal. These provenance declarations are attested records, not proof of independent people or independently verified runtime identity. The academic dissent is preserved below, and the remaining verification and placeholder steps are explicit merge conditions.
dissent: REV-PREM-SCI-004-ACADEMIC-E700B378 requested changes because the clinical wrap-up lacked same-scene evidence mapping and overstated what random order and reversibility alone could support. Both objections were accepted and incorporated; the original request-changes verdict remains part of the record.
